judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notices 'may be given' by any of several means and 'may be made orally, to be confirmed promptly in writing' — a permissive/mandatory mixture of exactly the kind courts construe, since it is unclear whether an oral notice is effective before written confirmation. 'Promptly' is a further soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to addresses 'specified in Annex II', and it governs the Paragraph 4 margin notices and the Paragraph 11(a) default notice, so the validity of a margin call made by telephone turns on this clause read with Paragraph 4(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is not a true integration clause: it supersedes only prior agreements 'containing general terms and conditions for repurchase transactions', leaving the reach of that phrase — and the status of other agreements — open. The severability sentence is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Paragraph 3(b) (Confirmations plus the Agreement are 'conclusive evidence') and the various Annex precedence clauses, the document's hierarchy is assembled from several partly overlapping rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment consent, binding-on-successors and termination all appear in one paragraph, but each sentence is definite and the survival carve-out for outstanding Transactions is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) expressly carves out Paragraph 11 receivables, and Paragraph 12's single-agreement concept is unaffected; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, clearly worded carve-out from the assignment prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a stated exception to 15(a) rather than a contradiction of it; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line New York choice of law excluding renvoi; about as definite as a clause gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I para 6 adds a non-exclusive Manhattan forum, which complements rather than conflicts with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-waiver and no-oral-modification clause with an express saver for missed margin notices; internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires writing signed by both parties for modification, which sits against Paragraph 3(a)'s oral Transactions and Paragraph 13's oral notices; those are different subject matters but the tension is worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ERISA notice and representation duties are stated plainly, and the last sentence's 'may proceed in reliance thereon but shall not be required so to proceed' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 18(b) is expressly 'subject to the last sentence of subparagraph (a)', so the two dovetail; Annex IV para 4(d) handles agent-side plan transactions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A condition precedent expressed in mandatory terms with a defined document set; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to 18(a)'s last sentence and is echoed by 18(c)'s continuing delivery undertaking; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'no material adverse change in Seller's financial condition' is a genuinely open standard, though it is a familiar one and is deemed rather than negotiated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A breach would feed Paragraph 11(vi)'s representation default, but only in Plan Party transactions; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double 'except insofar as' carve-outs make the recognition self-cancelling in the very cases where characterisation matters, which is an odd but deliberate structure. The statutory citation is garbled to 'Section 10 I' in this copy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Paragraph 6's sale-not-loan framing and 19(b)-(d); the carve-outs mean the parties' 'recognition' does not bind a court, which is a known limitation rather than an internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statement of understanding about safe-harbour liquidation rights; the mis-citation of 'Title II' for Title 11 is a transcription slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 11(d) and 19(a); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional recognition language with an express inapplicability carve-out; definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 19(a) and (d) and to Annex I para 5's FDICIA representation; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same pattern: a statutory characterisation subject to a carve-out if a party is not a 'financial institution'. Clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I para 5 requires each party to represent it is a financial institution or an EE-qualifying counterparty, which reduces the carve-out's bite; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure disclosure of a regulator's position, imposing no obligation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 20(b)-(c) and 19; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statutory disclosure; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside 20(a) and (c); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat disclosure that funds are not insured deposits; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 19(c)-(d) and 20(a)-(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It makes an enumerated set of annexes and schedules part of the Agreement, but the list is printed as a form list rather than tailored, and Schedule III.A still reads '[Relevant Country]'. The reach of the list is thus uncertain on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VII and Schedule VII.A are declared applicable although no Fund or Custodian is ever identified and Annex VII para 2 leaves the margin percentage blank, so the instrument makes applicable annexes it never populates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence priority rule; on its own it is clear, though 'this Annex' in a document containing seven annexes is a little loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives Annex I priority over the Agreement while Annex VI para 1 and Annex VII both claim to prevail over 'any other term of the Agreement', and Paragraph 11(d) defers to Annex I — a circular hierarchy that cannot be resolved from the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Purchase Price Maintenance' does not match the content, which is about Income payments, and the operative words 'the amount to be transferred to Buyer or Seller upon termination' misquote Paragraph 5(ii), which speaks only of amounts transferred to Buyer by Seller. That mismatch is a visible mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Buyer's Paragraph 5 election, but Paragraph 5's carve-outs (A) and (B) — margin deficit and continuing Event of Default — are not addressed, and Annex VI para 9 disapplies Paragraph 5 altogether for Buy/Sell Backs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantially the same Securities' is a genuinely vague standard, and the closing sentence 'Buyer shall offer Seller the right to terminate the Transaction' leaves the terms and consequences of that termination unstated. The notice timing sentence is also self-contradictory about whether notice after 10:00 a.m. is permitted at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grafts a Seller substitution right onto Paragraph 9(a), which requires Buyer's agreement, and onto 9(b)'s deemed acceptance in custody transactions; reconciling the three requires work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cost formula ends with 'the loss incurred by Buyer directly arising or resulting from such substitution or termination' to be 'solely determined and calculated by Buyer in good faith' — a one-sided discretion whose limits are exactly what a court construes. 'Actual cost' versus hypothetical hedge costs is a further open point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Paragraph 11(g)'s default damages but applies to a non-default event, and it is triggered where 'Seller exercises its right to substitute or terminate' even though under 9(c) the termination right is offered by Buyer, not exercised by Seller.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch representation tracking Regulation EE; the terms are all externally defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports Paragraph 19(d)'s FDICIA characterisation; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Submission is to 'non-exclusive' jurisdiction yet 'solely for the purpose of' enforcement suits, a slightly awkward pairing, but the effect is conventional and permissive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Paragraph 16's New York governing law; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad, enumerated waiver of immunity; the parenthetical list is illustrative but the class is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Annex I para 6; irrelevant to these commercial parties but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long definitions block; 'International Security' and 'International Transaction' use broad disjunctive tests ('capable of being cleared through a clearing facility outside the United States') that could sweep in ordinary trades. That breadth is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Business Day' only for International Transactions while the main Agreement uses 'business day' throughout without definition, leaving the domestic meaning to be supplied from outside the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'LIBOR plus a spread, as may be specified' leaves the spread at zero or undetermined if nothing is specified, which is a real gap in a default-interest input.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 2(m) for International Transactions and feeds Paragraph 11(h)'s 'greater of' formula, so the gap has operative consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-branch transfer list ending in 'any other method mutually acceptable'; open-ended but mutual-consent limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels Paragraph 7 without contradicting it; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short default rule subject to mutual agreement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Qualified by 3(b)-(d) of the same Annex; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The discharge mechanic is stated with care ('consistent with normal banking procedures', 'customary delivery period'), and those two phrases are the only soft edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides 3(a) and feeds 3(c)/(d); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional currency-indemnity with a judgment non-merger clause; long but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its parenthetical carve-out for a nondefaulting party mirrors 3(d); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short refund obligation; 'promptly' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirror of 3(c); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line notices rule adding an English-language requirement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Incorporates Paragraph 13, whose oral-notice permission carries over; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Transfer taxes, stamp taxes and all similar costs' is a specific pair followed by a general 'all similar costs', so the catch-all's reach is uncertain. That is a textbook ejusdem generis point, if a small one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside the gross-up in 5(b)(i) and the Tax Event machinery in Paragraph 6; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed gross-up with a connection-based exclusion; dense but each element is defined, and 'for the avoidance of doubt' resolves the Income interaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly coordinates with Paragraph 5 of the Agreement and with Paragraph 6 of the Annex; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any certificate or document reasonably requested' is broad but bounded by reasonableness; the sentence is cut off in this copy but the sense is complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds 5(b)(iv)'s forfeiture of gross-up; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any circumstance known or reasonably known to it' is an awkward formulation but its sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Excludes Change of Tax Law as defined in Paragraph 6, dovetailing with that paragraph; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise cross-referenced exclusion from the gross-up; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5(b)(i)-(iii); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'material adverse effect ... in the notifying party's reasonable opinion' combines a vague standard with a subjective judgment, and the trigger includes any taxing-authority action anywhere. Nameable softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is answerable by the counter-notice in 6(d) and the opinion requirement in 6(b), which discipline it; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a suitably qualified adviser' is vague, but the consequence of a disagreement is limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports 6(a) and precedes 6(c) termination; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A termination right with a stated 30-day minimum notice and a nomination mechanic; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a Repurchase Date, which fits 2(q)'s definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The counter-notice deems an indemnity 'against the adverse effect' without quantifying it, which leaves the indemnity's measure open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 6(c)'s termination and restores the original Repurchase Date; internally coherent with 6(a)-(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An expense indemnity coupled with a bar on 'consequential loss or damage', a phrase whose boundary is perennially litigated. That term is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across Paragraph 11(g)'s broad damages entitlement, but only for Tax Event terminations, which is a drafted limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short without-prejudice saver; 'where appropriate' is loose but consequence-light.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates Paragraphs 5 and 6 of the Annex; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical conversion rule keyed to the defined Spot Rate; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It modifies the Paragraph 4 calculation for non-Base-Currency sums without disturbing it; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An additional default limb covering 'any covenant or obligation' under the Annex with a one-business-day cure; the 'including, without limitation' phrase is broad but the class is the whole Annex anyway.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside Paragraph 11's list, which gives no cure period for Paragraph 4 breaches, producing an uneven cure regime across default types.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A currency-conversion and setoff remedy exercisable 'at any time at its option'; broad but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly additive to Paragraph 11 rights and consistent with Paragraph 12's netting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope recital defining Agent and Principal; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex IV is declared applicable by Annex I para 1 even though both parties contracted as principals under Paragraph 10(ii), which is a mild fit question rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A continuing authority representation stated in ordinary terms; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly additional to Paragraph 10 and feeds Annex IV para 3's liability limitation; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rescission right turns on the other party's 'sole discretion' that Principals are 'not acceptable to it', a wholly subjective standard, and the unwind mechanics with two provisos are dense. The discretion is the nameable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its preservation of Price Differential on rescinded Transactions sits oddly with the notion that a rescinded Transaction never bound the parties; otherwise consistent with Annex IV paras 4 and 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limitation is conditioned on the representations being 'true and correct in all material respects' and on Agent otherwise complying — conditions whose satisfaction is exactly what would be fought over. Still, the drafting is orderly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts down Paragraph 12(ii)'s setoff right, which Annex IV para 5 expressly acknowledges; the two are drafted to fit.
